speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the characteristics of your neck swelling, such as whether it is painful, hard, or moving? When did you first notice this mass?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of colon cancer is very significant. Is this new swelling hard and fixed, or does it feel soft and mobile? Also, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or breathing?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Colon Cancer to the Neck. Given your history of colon cancer and the new, painless, progressive swelling on the nape of your neck, this is highly suspicious for metastatic disease. I need to confirm this immediately with imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_CTA.
